newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania parliament approves new state oil firm.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania parliament approves new state oil firm.

text.p: The Lithuanian parliament on Tuesday backed the formation of a national oil company to be formed out of the merger of an oil terminal, a refinery, a service station network and a pipeline operator.
The initial share capital of the company is estimated at 790 million litas ($197 million) and the government says the formation of the company will help attract foreign investment.
The parliament press service said 42 members of the 141-seat parliament voted for the motion to form Lietuvos Nafta (Lithuanian Oil) and 32 voted against.
The firm is to be a holding company that will own the Mazheikiu Nafta oil refinery, the planned Butinge oil terminal, the Lietuvos Kuras service station network and the Naftotiekis pipeline.
The state has to hold at least 51 percent of the new company for three years but can then bring its share down to 34 percent.
